messages:
maria: Heads-up — proposing we lift the runtime pin for 2.19.0 so SDK 1.9 can enable the new op_conv kernel for quant-v5 models. Need a quick canary plan and rollback criteria.
jin: curious — what's the driver? perf or correctness?
maria: both. op_conv cuts P95 token latency by ~18% on our bench for small batch gen, but we saw a rare mismatch with fused attention on long sequences in local tests (not reproducing consistently).
eli: thanks for the context. If we unpin, we should gate by: 1) canary at 5-10% traffic, 2) monitor OOM and p95/p99 latency, 3) compare evalset outputs for divergence > epsilon, and 4) auto-roll back if error-rate > 0.5% for 10m.
sara: agree. add a QA run against the regression testset (prompt-suite/regress-v2) within the canary window. If any semantic regressions > 0.02 BLEU on the eval set, abort.
maria: sounds good. proposed schedule: start canary in us-west2 at 09:30 UTC for 2 hours, then expand to us-central at 50% if green, full unpin at EOD.
ops: note — Dedicated customers pinned to runtime 2.18 will not be affected. Private deployments only change if they opt-in.
jin: what about deploybot commands? can we do an automated staged rollout?
maria: yes — deploybot has a rollout script. command to run: ```/deploybot rollout runtime 2.19.0 --canary 10 --region us-west2 --watch 1200``` 
deploybot: @maria — Received rollout request. Starting canary orchestration. Link: https://deploy.redwood.internal/rollouts/rl-3509876543
qa-bot: QA run queued: regress-v2 suite against runtime 2.19.0. ETA ~12m. Results will post to the thread.
sara: also add a tracing hook: instrument tokenization and KV cache hit rate so we can see if op_conv interacts with our cache eviction pattern.
eli: adding metric alerts: p95 latency > baseline + 12% for 5m, OOM spikes > +2 occurrences in 15m, error-rate > 0.5%. If triggered, deploybot will execute rollback.
maria: rollback playbook reminder: ```/deploybot rollback runtime 2.19.0 --reason "canary-failure"``` + remove pinlist entry for canary if we abort. ops — please ensure runbook is reachable.
ops: runbook link pinned to incident channel; I've also uploaded a quick checklist to the docs page: https://docs.redwood.internal/release/runbooks/runtime-unpin-2-19
deploybot: Canary started: 10% traffic to us-west2. ID rl-3509876543. Watching for alerts.
qa-bot: regress-v2 initial pass complete — 1 semantic diff flagged (BLEU drop 0.018) on a long-seq prompt. Marked as flaky; will re-run with larger sample.
jin: that BLEU drop is close to threshold, we should watch. can we isolate by forcing no-KV-cache on that case?
maria: good idea. @eli can you run a targeted test disabling KV cache to see if it reproduces?
eli: running targeted job now. command: ```ci/test-runtime --model quant-v5 --runtime 2.19.0 --no-kv-cache --prompt-file tests/longseq-samples.txt``` 
ops: FYI latency graph: p95 +9% so far, error-rate stable at 0.12%. No OOM.
qa-bot: re-run complete — the BLEU diff disappears when KV cache disabled. That points to interaction with cache eviction path.
sara: then we should not widen the canary until we understand cache interaction. Recommend pausing expansion and opening a short RFC with suggested fixes.
maria: agreed. pausing rollout. deploybot — pause canary.
deploybot: Canary rl-3509876543 paused at 10% per request by @maria.
eli: I'll bisect the change set in op_conv + KV cache heuristics. ETA 4h if nothing weird shows up.
jin: tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for visibility. @ops let me know if you want to trigger an emergency rollback; current criteria haven't fired.
ops: will standby. posting a note in #incidents if thresholds trip.
maria: next steps: 1) eli to bisect & propose patch, 2) QA to re-run regress-v2 after fix, 3) if green, resume canary with same window; if not, rollback and add a compatibility note to the runtime pinlist. I'll draft the release note language.
sara: small ask — include the canary id and exact test commands in the release notes so SREs can audit later.
maria: will do. draft (wip): "Attempted runtime unpin to enable SDK 1.9 op_conv kernel (quant-v5). Canary paused due to KV-cache interaction on long sequences; rollback not triggered. Investigating fix."
